title: Simple constraints rarely force complex behavior, unlike simple rules

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Simple constraints rarely force complex behavior, unlike simple rules

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Unlike simple evolution rules, almost all simple constraints lead only to fairly simple patterns; complex behavior forced by constraints is rare.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it seems that almost all simple constraints lead only to fairly simple patterns.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 5, “Two Dimensions and Beyond”; section “Systems Based on Constraints” (from p. 210), p. 221. Scope: constraint-based systems compared with rule-based simple programs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch05-21: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Large finite catalogs permit informative comparisons after substantial interpretation. The broad “almost all” conclusion is representation-dependent and cannot be settled across unspecified formalisms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Choose matched finite grammars of constraints and evolution rules, a sampling measure, and complexity metrics for their generated patterns, then compare the frequency of high-complexity outcomes. The claim is supported only if the result is robust across reasonable encodings and metrics.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Pattern complexity has competing definitions.

Rule and constraint formalisms are difficult to match fairly.

No canonical measure over “simple” systems.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.38
data existence: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.4

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both sides of the comparison can be sampled: small template constraints by search, and elementary rules by direct evolution. The sentence is a rate claim about almost all simple constraints, and any finite sample leaves the tail, the complexity cutoff, and the matching of the two ensembles open. It can support or challenge a stated proxy, not the unrestricted quantifier.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fix finite ensembles of small constraints and of small cellular-automaton rules, score each output as repetitive, nested, or complex by pre-registered tests, and compare the two rates. A constraint rate of complex outcomes comparable to the rule rate would challenge the contrast inside those ensembles.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The text already allows rare complex constraints, so only the rate is at issue.

Constraint spaces and rule spaces are different sets, so raw rates are not automatically comparable.

Almost all, simple, and fairly simple each depend on the ensemble and the complexity score.
